explanation: Collect the original nodes into an array, then build a reference order by alternating the leftmost and rightmost remaining entries. Relink that order and terminate the last node. No node value is moved or replaced.
timeComplexity: O(n): collect n nodes, select each node once into the alternating order, then rewrite n links.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space for the collected references and reordered reference array; original data nodes are reused.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: After i iterations the order contains the first i and last i original nodes in the required alternating order. The two indices enclose exactly the unused nodes; adding the middle only once handles odd lengths. Relinking this permutation preserves every node and places L0 first.
walkthrough: Collect [8,2,7,1,6]. Choose array endpoints 8,6, then 2,1, then middle 7 once. Relink as 8→6→2→1→7→null. The method returns no value; the wrapper follows the original head and displays [8,6,2,1,7]. The callable returns no value; expected follows next links from the original head, and the harness additionally checks original-node identities and values.
edgeCases: Empty and singleton lists need no relinking.
Odd lengths retain one final middle node.
The head object and all original node values remain unchanged.
